Hi Karthik,

We're seeing an odd failure on a handful of our supplier activations (TempAcct). After the supplier completes the DocuSign step, the link redirects them back to the portal but they immediately hit a login loop: the accept screen reloads and shows "Session expired" then sends them back into the DocuSign flow. It happens on both desktop and mobile (iOS Safari).

Attached: tempack_docusign-confirm.pdf (DocuSign envelope confirmation) and screenshot_login_loop.png (mobile repro).

Quick details that might help:
- Supplier account email: vendor+tempacct@tempack.co
- DocuSign envelope: 0a1b2c3d4e (attached)
- Happening for 3 suppliers in the last 24 hours

Can you advise next steps? We're trying to close the onboarding this week and this loop is blocking PO visibility.

Thanks,
Laura (on behalf of Tempack Ops)

Hi Laura — thanks for the details and attachments. Sorry you're blocked; we'll prioritize this.

Immediate ask: can you confirm the timestamp (local to the user) when they completed the DocuSign step for one affected supplier? That helps us correlate logs. Also please confirm whether the supplier used a mobile deep-link from the DocuSign email or tapped the accept link in the portal.

Proposed mutual action plan (quick):
- Ben to instrument the session token handoff on our end and confirm whether the one-time token is being consumed by DocuSign redirect twice. (ETA: 2 business hours)
- Tempack to share one example timestamp + full DocuSign envelope id (you shared 0a1b2c3d4e, which helps).
- If we confirm double consume, we can push a short TTL bump for the one-time activation token for affected envs and provide a manual admin session reset instruction for operators to unblock current accounts.

I've looped in Ben (Runtime) for the first-pass investigation. Marissa, can you pull any recent onboarding audit entries for vendor+tempacct@tempack.co so we have the admission events?

I'll create a support ticket and share updates there as well.

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Tempack Ops <ops@tempack.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Supplier TempAcct - activation flows failing after DocuSign

Thanks, Karthik & Laura — I dug into the runtime logs for the envelope id you provided. Observations:

1) We see the one-time activation token issued by the portal at 2028-06-14T16:02:33Z and a redirect callback from DocuSign at 2028-06-14T16:02:34Z that consumes the token (expected).
2) Then we see a second inbound request from the same client at 2028-06-14T16:02:35Z that attempts to re-use the same activation token and gets rejected -> session reset -> redirect back to accept page (this matches the loop).
3) The second request originates from a mobile UA string that suggests DocuSign's in-app browser on iOS is replaying the callback once more when it tries to open the external deep-link.

Workaround to unblock current accounts (admin steps):
- Karthik or Tempack admin: from the Admin -> Sessions panel, locate the pending activation for vendor+tempacct@tempack.co and perform a "Force session reset". That will clear the stuck state and allow the supplier to complete a fresh activation.
- I can provide a short script to surface pending activations filtered by envelope id if helpful.

Longer term fix options:
- Increase one-time activation token TTL from 60s to 180s for the tenant that Tempack uses (low risk for fraud since token is single-use and bound to envelope id).
- Add detection for consecutive callback attempts within 2s from the same client UA and treat the second attempt as a no-op instead of invalidating the session.

I will open INC-78234 and attach log excerpts. In the meantime, please try the admin reset and report back the timestamp you performed it.

Command to list pending activations (internal):
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_API_KEY" "https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/activations?envelope=0a1b2c3d4e"

Attaching initial log snippet and will push an SOP for the reset flow shortly.

— Ben
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
